newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says China's Spratly ships reported gone.
newsitem.headline: Manila says China's Spratly ships reported gone.

text.p: Philippines Defence Secretary Renato de Villa said on Friday he had received reports that armed Chinese ships in an area claimed by Manila in the Spratly islands had pulled out.

"There is an aerial reconnaissance in the area... As of yesterday we have reports they have vacated the area. We are verifying that today. Before the day is over, we will get a report from the (local military command)," he told reporters.

After de Villa's comments, an Air Force official told Reuters that reconaissance flights by two Nomad planes on Thursday failed to find any sign of the ships, which the Philippines said they had first sighted on April 25 near two islands occupied by Philippine soldiers.
"There are no more ships in the area. We could not find them any more," the official said.
Manila has lodged a protest with Beijing after spotting three armed Chinese ships, accompanied by fishing boats, near the islands.
The Spratlys are a cluster of barely habitable isles, reefs and shoals in the South China Sea with no obvious value but are believed to be sitting on potentially rich oil and gas deposits.
